{"id": "e83bf705-0acb-4bc8-9973-b67f0ece399d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Yes, the logs never expire, but the cost is tiny at your current volume.**

**What I found**
- Bedrock invocation logging in us-east-1 delivers only to the CloudWatch log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. There is no S3 destination, so no S3 lifecycle rules apply.
- The log group has **no retention policy**, so it uses the default "never expire". Storage grows for as long as you keep invoking models.
- It's a Standard-class log group, created around Oct 16, 2026. It currently holds about **127 MB**.

**Cost**
- That works out to about 3 MB/day, or roughly 90–95 MB/month.
- Standard storage is about $0.03 per GB-month, so you're paying well under a cent per month for storage. A year of logs at this rate would be about 1.1 GB, or roughly $0.03/month.
- This is a rough estimate. The stored-bytes figure can lag, and the storage price is from memory. I didn't look up current pricing.
- For Bedrock logging, **ingestion** (about $0.50/GB) is usually the bigger line item than storage. It's a one-time charge per byte and retention doesn't change it.
- The volume could jump if you start sending large prompts or responses, or higher traffic. Text delivery is on, and the config also enables video data delivery. That's worth knowing if you ever use video models.

**Recommendation**
Set a retention period on the log group, for example 30, 90, or 365 days, depending on your audit needs. That caps storage growth for good. If you need longer-term retention, you could also export or subscribe the logs to S3.

I can't set the retention policy myself. Applying it is a write operation that I may only be able to run with your approval. You can also run it yourself with `aws logs put-retention-policy`.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
